qt: to the Commission Christel Schaldemose (S&D) Subject:

Automatic Content Recognition (ACR) is one of the ways in which smart TVs gather information on users’ viewing habits. LG has stated that the technology has been rolled out in a number of European countries1. ACR uses audio fingerprinting to identify content on the TV, and that information can be used for target-group segmentation and audience behaviour analysis, among other things. LG maintains that ACR is deactivated by default and activated only when the user accepts the company’s Viewing Information Agreement2. After that, LG can process information on content, devices and networks, etc. Under certain conditions, it can share information with LG Ad Solutions. This raises questions about consumers’ insight into and control over data collection, as well as the enforcement of EU data protection rules. With the above in mind: 1.

Does the Commission have an overview of the scope and nature of the data collection that smart TV manufacturers – including LG and Samsung – are carrying out in the EU using ACR, among other technologies?
How does the Commission assess whether this practice is in line with EU data protection rules, including the requirements regarding transparency and valid grounds for processing?
Does the Commission take the view that oversight of such data collection is sufficient, and if not, will the Commission take steps to ensure more effective enforcement?
